LESSON: WEATHER

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Natural Environment
Topic 2.1: Weather
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Weather, part of Natural Environment in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why do we need to predict weather?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Weather together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Unity: learner develops cooperation as they observe and record prevailing weather conditions as an outdoor activity.

● Integrity: learner develops honesty as they observe and record weather conditions over a period of one week.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Life skills: learner develops effective communication skills when participating in a class contest, on narrating weather occurrences for a

past week from weather chart recordings.

● Learner support programs: learner develops career guidance skills when creating a weather record using weather symbols for a period

of one week.

Link to other subject:

Drawing weather symbols relates to the skill of drawing and colouring in Creative Activities.

Suggested learning resources

Approved support learning materials, local environment, flash cards, braille cards, resource person, weather charts in print and braille, pictures,

digital devices with assistive technology.
